source.description: Self-reported benchmark results extracted from 50 official model release documents (system cards, model cards, technical reports, release posts) by the 2026-09-15 scout job. The job is a lead: every value ingested here is re-verified against our own capture of the primary document.

rules: Only rows whose basis_hint is vendor_claim_own_model are ingested. A lab's number for a competitor (vendor_claim_about_other_model) is context, not evidence; a number a lab quotes from an independent board (secondary_quote) is taken from that board instead.

A row is ingested only when its (benchmark_normalized, benchmark_version) pair appears in `accepted` below, so the benchmark identity a lab printed is matched to one registry identity explicitly and never by name similarity.

Every value is re-verified against our own bounded capture of the primary document: the printed benchmark row must exist on the page the locator names, and the document's own comparison values must line up with the claimed column. A row that fails is rejected with its reason, never silently dropped.
basis is always self_reported. These values never enter the Composite and never replace a measured result; the product marks them as reported by the developer.
comparison_key stays null: a vendor's own harness and the board's harness are not a reviewed compatible pair, so no divergence is computed from these rows.
An unresolved catalog identity stays unmatched (model_id null) instead of being guessed onto a reasoning variant.

A candidate an independent critic did not clear is listed in `withheld` with the objection and is not ingested. It stays a rejected candidate with its reason, so the next round can take it up again; an unresolved objection is never resolved by the producer alone.

accepted.rationale: SWE-bench Verified is one published 500-task set with one metric (% resolved). Labs run it with their own scaffold, which the protocol string records. Established precedent in this registry: the Devstral 2 and DeepSeek V3 vendor claims already sit on this identity.
Same shape as SWE-bench Verified: one published task set of multilingual repositories, one % resolved metric, and the vendor scaffold recorded in the protocol.
Same shape as SWE-bench Verified: one published task set of issues with image context, one % resolved metric, and the vendor scaffold recorded in the protocol.
Only the literal version 4.0 joins the 4.0 identity. Terminal-Bench 2.0, 2.1, 3.0 and 'Hard' are different task sets and have no neutral registry identity of their own yet, so those rows stay out.
LongBench v2 is a fixed 503-question multiple-choice set. Precedent: the DeepSeek V3 vendor claim already sits on this identity.
Precedent: the DeepSeek V3 vendor claim already sits on this identity.
Vending-Bench 2 reports a final balance in USD; the registry unit is USD and the published version is literal.
Precedent: the Qwen3 vendor claims already sit on this identity, with the domain (retail / airline / telecom) recorded in the protocol.

excluded.reason: The HLE identity a lab prints is regularly ambiguous — full set, text-only subset, with or without tools. This registry already rejected a Qwen HLE row for exactly that reason. Needs a per-document identity review before any of these rows can be ingested.

The registry has no neutral GPQA Diamond identity: aa-gpqa-diamond is Artificial Analysis' implementation and openrouter-gpqa-diamond is OpenRouter's own run. A lab's own GPQA Diamond run is a third implementation and would need its own identity.

These registry identities freeze one operator's own run (Datacurve, Cursor, Cognition, Scale AI, Artificial Analysis). A lab running the same benchmark itself is a different implementation, which the registry keeps separate. Ingesting these needs a new registry identity for the benchmark's own published protocol, with its own primary source.
Our identity is the SWE-Bench Pro *public* set. The release documents print 'SWE-bench Pro' without stating the set, so which one was run is unverified. Revisit per document.

withheld.reason: The independent critic did not clear this value in two review rounds. Its reasoning was self-contradictory (it stated the character-column alignment puts 86.6 under 'Fable 5' and still recorded a finding), so this is withheld rather than corrected: an unresolved objection is not the same as a confirmed defect. Re-review with a fresh packet before ingesting.

Critic objection, not cleared: the column anchor relies on a header 56 lines above the row in a folded HTML table. The alignment holds, but the evidence was called weak; withheld until a review clears it.
Critic objection, not cleared: the published row prints the same value twice (69.3), so the critic would not accept the column attribution from the evidence shown. Withheld until a review clears it.
